name: topo_pen_hover_target
description: Topology Pen P1 (doc/topopen_p1_plan.md): the constraint layer's `resolveHoverTarget` (source/constraint.d), probed end-to-end through GET /api/surface-raycast's `targetKind`/`targetVert`/`targetEdge` fields. Builds on the P0 'focus-point trick' (see topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's provenance) -- every case's camera `focus` lands the raycast hit EXACTLY at that world point, at the viewport CENTRE pixel (475,300). All expected numbers (including the threshold-flip cases' projected pixel distances) are derived analytically from vibe3d's own documented camera formulas (sphericalToCartesian / lookAt / perspectiveMatrix / projectToWindowFull, math.d + view.d) via a standalone (uncommitted) Python replica of those formulas -- the SAME method topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's author used, not a call into resolveHoverTarget itself. No reference 3D modeling tool was used (P1's resolution rule is an explicit PLACEHOLDER, not a claim of reference parity -- see case 9 and doc/topopen_p1_plan.md's Deferred section). P2 CORRECTION (doc/topopen_p2_plan.md): every case here drives the raycast oracle through a real camera + `geometry` argstring, exactly like topo_pen_surface_raycast.json -- these are camera-ray (Screen-mode) hit resolutions, not synthetic-packet calls (those live separately as constraint.d's own `makeHoverTestViewport` module unittests, run under `dub test`). Originally authored under `geometry point` back when P0's raycast branch always did a camera-ray search regardless of mode; relabeled `geometry screen` here for the same reason and with the same byte-identical-values guarantee as topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's relabel.

provenance.method: hand + independent Python re-derivation of math.d/view.d (sphericalToCartesian, lookAt, perspectiveMatrix, projectToWindowFull)
provenance.notes: Most cases use an az=0/el=0 camera (eye = focus + (0,0,distance), forward = -Z) or az=pi/2/el=0 (forward = -X) so the camera's rotation is axis-aligned with a face the case tests head-on -- for any offset confined to that face's own plane (zero depth-component relative to the camera), the perspective projection collapses to an EXACT uniform pixel scale S = (1+sqrt(2)) * 0.5 * viewportHeight / distance (viewportHeight=544 for the default --test window), independent of which in-plane direction the offset points. Cases 5/6 (threshold_wide_vertex / threshold_narrow_face) use this to hand-derive the corner's exact projected distance from the hit point: offset (0.15,0.15,0) at distance=5 -> S=131.3332 px/unit -> corner pixel distance = S*0.15*sqrt(2) = 27.860px, nearest-edge pixel distance = S*0.15 = 19.700px (both independently verified against the standalone Python replica, not against resolveHoverTarget's own output). Case 9 (vertex_beats_edge) uses the same face/camera with a smaller offset (0.03,0.03,0): vertex=5.572px, edge=3.940px -- BOTH inside the default 12px radius, so the PLACEHOLDER Vertex>Edge precedence (not the reference editor's real precedence -- deferred to C2/P4) is what picks 'vertex' despite the edge being the geometrically closer candidate. Cases 4 and 10 reuse topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's 'ray_miss' and 'bg_hidden_not_hit' camera/geometry verbatim (already-verified misses, now both `screen`). All 10 cases relabeled `geometry point` -> `geometry screen` for P2 (doc/topopen_p2_plan.md): every camera here is an axis-aligned head-on view whose auto work-plane and camera-ray direction are NOT generally coincident, so under the corrected Point-mode (nearest-foot-from-work-plane-seed) semantics these same setups would resolve to DIFFERENT hit points than the camera-ray hit these values were derived against -- Screen mode is the honest label for what these cases actually exercise.

cases.name: vertex_snap_corner
cases._comment: Cube top face (face 4, Y=0.5 plane); focus sits 0.04 world units (X and Z) short of corner (0.5,0.5,0.5) -- independently computed corner pixel distance ~6.05px, comfortably inside the default 12px radius (the incident edges are even closer -- 3.95/5.75px -- but Vertex has priority regardless).

cases.name: edge_snap_boundary
cases._comment: Planar quad at Y=0; focus sits 0.1 world units inside the boundary edge (10,0,10)-(10,0,-10) (a point EXACTLY on that edge is numerically borderline for the BVH raycast -- the ray can miss the mesh entirely at that precise boundary, so the focus is nudged just inside), ~10 world units from either corner -- independently computed corner pixel distances (~93px, ~165px) are far outside the default 12px radius, and the edge distance (~0.1 world units, sub-pixel at this camera's scale) is far below it vs ~149px for the quad's diagonal.

cases.name: face_point_interior
cases._comment: Cube top face, focus near the face centre -- independently computed distances to every corner (70-125px) and every boundary edge (48-76px) are all far outside the default 12px radius, so the hit resolves to a free face-point (no vert/edge).

cases.name: off_surface_none
cases._comment: Reuses topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's 'ray_miss' camera/geometry verbatim (already-verified miss) -- no surface hit at all, so hover resolution must be None regardless of threshold.

cases.name: threshold_wide_vertex
cases._comment: REV-C: SAME camera+geometry as threshold_narrow_face, only thresholdPx differs. Cube face1 (Z=0.5 plane) viewed head-on (az=0,el=0 -> forward=-Z, an EXACT axis-aligned projection for any offset confined to this Z=const face). focus=(0.35,0.35,0.5) is 0.15 world units short of corner (0.5,0.5,0.5) in both X and Z. Independently derived (see suite provenance): S = (1+sqrt2)*0.5*544/5 = 131.3332 px/world-unit; corner pixel distance = S*0.15*sqrt(2) = 27.860px. thresholdPx=60 puts that corner INSIDE the radius -> vertex.

cases.name: threshold_narrow_face
cases._comment: REV-C: SAME camera+geometry as threshold_wide_vertex -- only thresholdPx differs (60 -> 4). Independently derived (see suite provenance): corner pixel distance = 27.860px, nearest-edge pixel distance = 19.700px. thresholdPx=4 puts BOTH candidates outside the radius -> face. Margins: 27.86-4=23.86px (vertex), 19.70-4=15.70px (edge) -- comfortably outside sub-pixel sampling error.

cases.name: multi_bg_nearer_vertex
cases._comment: Two background planes (PlaneHigh y=2 nearer to the camera, PlaneLow y=0 further) -- the raycast's nearest-wins rule (P0) must pick PlaneHigh, and the hover resolution must use ITS corner (10,2,10), not PlaneLow's geometry. focus=(9.95,2,9.95) is 0.05 short of the corner in both X,Z -- independently computed corner pixel distance ~6.76px (well inside the default 12px radius); the corner's two incident edges are ~4.6/5.4px (closer still, but Vertex wins by priority regardless).

cases.name: edge_snap_cube_side
cases._comment: Direction diversity: cube +X side (face 3, X=0.5 plane) viewed head-on along -X (az=pi/2, el=0 -> forward=-X, the same axis-aligned-projection trick as cases 5/6/9 but on a different axis, avoiding the az=el=0 gimbal case's Z-only coverage). focus sits EXACTLY on the midpoint of the top edge of that face -- independently computed corner distances ~82px each (far outside the default 12px radius), edge distance 0 (on it).

cases.name: vertex_beats_edge
cases._comment: PLACEHOLDER precedence (deferred to C2/P4 -- see doc/topopen_p1_plan.md's Deferred section): cube face1 (Z=0.5), same head-on camera as cases 5/6, focus 0.03 world units short of corner (0.5,0.5,0.5) in both X and Z. Independently derived (see suite provenance): vertex pixel distance = 5.572px, incident-edge pixel distance = 3.940px -- the EDGE is geometrically CLOSER, but resolveHoverTarget checks Vertex first and both are inside the default 12px radius, so 'vertex' wins. This is NOT a claim that the reference editor's real precedence prefers vertex over a closer edge -- it is this phase's explicit placeholder rule, replaced by a captured precedence in P4.

cases.name: bg_hidden_none
cases._comment: Reuses topo_pen_surface_raycast.json's 'bg_hidden_not_hit' camera/geometry verbatim -- the background layer is hidden (layer.setVisible false), so there is no surface hit at all and hover resolution must be None.
